decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Add ... bookmarks (URL...)” and “empty-URL validation (returns `400`)”. Client round 1: “I can save ... bookmarks.”
decisions.note: Implementation-review presentation records URL-based creation with the required URL enforced.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents the editable fields as “URL, title, description, tags,” omitting the required note field. Client round 1 gives only general approval: “I can ... edit ... bookmarks. I’m happy with the app.”
decisions.note: The implementation-review field set diverges from the required editable fields. The client does not mention the missing note field or explicitly accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Add / edit / delete bookmarks”. Client round 1: “I can ... remove bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The presented delete capability conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 specifies “title defaults to the URL” and separately says favicons load from Google’s favicon service; it does not present automatic collection of the target title, description, and preview image. Client round 1 responds only that saving is covered and the app is satisfactory.
decisions.note: The presented save-time metadata behavior differs from automatic collection of all four required metadata elements. General approval does not surface or explicitly accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “Comma-separated tags” and bookmarks support “tags”. Client round 1: “I can ... organize ... bookmarks.”
decisions.note: The presentation records assignment of multiple tags and therefore conforms at implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “sidebar tag cloud + counts; click a tag to filter” and API support for “?tag=” filtering. Client round 1 generally approves the app.
decisions.note: Clicking a specific tag to filter its bookmarks is a functionally conforming implementation.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 defines search scope as “title, URL, description, and tags,” omitting bookmark notes. Client round 1 says only “I can ... find ... bookmarks” and approves the app.
decisions.note: The explicitly presented search field set lacks the required note search. The response neither identifies nor explicitly accepts that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 states, “Let me know if you’d like ... an import/export (browser bookmarks) ... added,” establishing that this capability is not currently included. Client round 1 gives broad final approval without mentioning import or export.
decisions.note: At implementation review, the bundled import/export option is explicitly deferred rather than implemented. The client does not state the expected Netscape HTML behavior or explicitly accept its absence.
